scope: Exact actor-key/task-code source delta. A removed finding is not a completed actor, new gameplay implementation, artistic approval or 1:1 certification.

incarnation.after: Dead Space 3 (2013), John Carver in military RIG

visualAnchor.after: Adult John Carver wears his bulky dark military RIG with red illuminated eye lenses and a blue/cyan spinal health strip. A physical modular military rifle is carried in both hands; no Isaac engineering helmet, Marker body growth or weapon made of hallucinations.

after.name: Tir du fusil militaire de Carver

incarnation.after: Dead Space 2 (2011), Ellie Langford in civilian pilot workwear

visualAnchor.after: Adult Ellie has dark hair tied back, pale sleeveless work top, brown utility trousers and practical boots. Use the living civilian pilot model of the Sprawl era; no Dead Space 3 winter coat or Isaac-style engineering RIG. Scene-specific eye state must be checked against the selected shot before art approval.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), Zach Hammond; retained historical duplicate actor ID

visualAnchor.after: This separate historical roster slot depicts the same living 2008 security chief Zach Hammond: adult Black man, close-cropped hair, brown security RIG, blue spinal lamps and physical Pulse Rifle. It is not a new character, ghost, remake model or merged save identity.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), Isaac Clarke and level-3 engineering RIG

visualAnchor.after: Original 2008 Isaac wears the bronze-brown level-3 engineering RIG with heavy segmented ribs, enclosed helmet, three cyan visor bars and a cyan spinal health strip. Hold the 211-V Plasma Cutter as a separate engineering tool; no remake redesign, Advanced Suit or Arctic suit.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), original Kendra Daniels

visualAnchor.after: Original 2008 Kendra is an adult human woman with a short dark bob, practical grey-blue technical jumpsuit and a small handheld diagnostic pad. No remake face/costume, military RIG, conjured energy weapon or offensive terminal lightning.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), living human medical officer Nicole Brennan

visualAnchor.after: Nicole is a living human medical officer in the original 2008 context, with loosely tied auburn/light-brown hair and practical grey-blue medical clothing. An ordinary datapad may support clinical instructions; no ghost glow, Marker lesions, summoned console or healing beam.

after.name: Refuge dans le poste médical Ishimura

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), security chief Zach Hammond

visualAnchor.after: Original 2008 Zach Hammond is an adult Black man with close-cropped hair, dark brown security RIG and blue spinal lights. Carry the SWS Motorized Pulse Rifle; no remake model, Isaac engineering helmet or 211-V Plasma Cutter mislabeled as his rifle.

after.name: Tir du Pulse Rifle de Hammond
Rafale du Pulse Rifle de Hammond

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), armored Brute form

visualAnchor.after: Very large hunched humanoid Brute with broad organic frontal armor, massive forearms and comparatively small rear legs. Preserve its organic plating and vulnerable shoulder/back regions; no metal knight armor, gun turret or Payday Bulldozer identity.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), Divider form

visualAnchor.after: Very tall thin humanoid Divider with stretched torso, small head and long spindly limbs that can separate into independently moving components. No bulky Brute armor, gun, or invented magic splitting staff.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), Exploder form

visualAnchor.after: Thin asymmetrical humanoid Exploder with one ordinary clawed arm and one conspicuously large yellow explosive pustule hanging from the other side. Its sac detonates; it is not an acid-spitting organ or a carried grenade launcher.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), Infector form

visualAnchor.after: Broad low Infector with a flattened torso, two large membranous wing-like limbs and a projecting infection proboscis. It works on corpses; no Slasher scythes, adult humanoid gun stance or Resident Evil T-Virus equipment.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), standard Leaper

visualAnchor.after: Low elongated Leaper with thick supporting forearms and a long bladed tail replacing ordinary lower-body locomotion. Preserve the long tail and forearm-driven leaps; no upright human stride, wings or humanoid weapon.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), standard Leaper

visualAnchor.after: Leaper has a low horizontal human-derived body, powerful forearms and a long hooked/barbed tail; its lower limbs are fused into the tail form. Keep the crawling/leaping anatomy without demon horns, wings, human running legs or a carried sword.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), original Lurker crawler

visualAnchor.after: Small original Lurker with a compact low crawler body and three independently raised organic tentacles ending in projectile spines. Preserve the three-tentacle silhouette; no adult soldier RIG, quadruped animal model from another installment or mechanical turret.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), standard human Slasher

visualAnchor.after: Original human Slasher with an emaciated humanoid torso, elongated bladed forelimbs, residual human legs and ragged civilian/workwear remnants. Scythe denotes its organic arm blades, not a carried medieval scythe or demonic armor.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), Pregnant form

visualAnchor.after: Large heavy humanoid Necromorph with a swollen abdomen, thick body and long bladed forearms. The abdomen contains separate Swarmers; no explosive yellow Exploder sac, infant Lurker body or firearm.

incarnation.after: Dead Space (2008), standard Slasher

visualAnchor.after: Human-derived Slasher with a narrow upright torso, extremely long organic arm blades and torn civilian/work clothes, moving on human-derived legs. Do not substitute an armored military variant, a Divider or generic clawed demon.

incarnation.after: Doom (1993) - classic Imp (TROO)

visualAnchor.after: Classic Doom brown leathery Imp: lean hunched humanoid, two clawed arms and two legs, small red eyes, open dark mouth with ivory teeth, short pale shoulder, elbow and knee spikes. No large head horns, tail, clothing, armor or Doom 2016/Eternal redesign. A_TroopAttack uses claws in melee range and a TROOPSHOT fireball at distance.

incarnation.after: Doom II (1994) - classic Mancubus (FATT)

visualAnchor.after: Classic Doom II Mancubus: very wide squat brown/tan folded body, short thick legs and small clawed feet, small bald head and green eyes. Two heavy gray forearm cannons replace the hands, with dark shoulder/back hoses and red connectors. No chest armor, held rifle, jetpack, shoulder rocket launchers or Doom 2016/Eternal redesign. A_FatAttack1/2/3 fire three two-projectile volleys; the existing six-contact signature keeps adapted Nexus timing and balance.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 3 (2011), Anya Stroud in frontline COG armor

visualAnchor.after: Adult blonde Anya in practical grey-blue COG combat armor with cyan lamps, dark underlayers and a physical Lancer Mk2. This is her frontline Gears 3 model, not the Gears 1 radio-room uniform or a later memorial image.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 2 (2008), young Damon Baird in COG field armor

visualAnchor.after: Young adult Baird with short blond hair, goggles resting on his forehead, grey-blue COG armor and cyan lamps. He carries a physical Lancer and ordinary maintenance tools; no old-man beard, Fabricator, autonomous turret or later-era robot.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 3 (2011), specifically adult Clayton Carmine

visualAnchor.after: Clayton Carmine has a fully closed opaque COG helmet, grey-blue heavy armor, blue lamps and conspicuously muscular bare arms. Carry a Lancer Mk2; do not substitute Anthony, Benjamin, Gary or Lizzie, their helmets, sleeves or eras.

after.name: Visée du Lancer Mk2 de Clayton
Garde du casque COG de Clayton
Rafale du Lancer de Clayton Carmine

incarnation.after: Gears of War 2 (2008), Augustus Cole in original Delta Squad armor

visualAnchor.after: Adult Black, muscular Augustus Cole with close-cropped hair, broad exposed arms, grey-blue COG armor and blue lights. Physical Lancer and Gnasher remain separate from his former Thrashball role; no Thrashball uniform or dialogue turned into projectiles.

before.name: Cole Train Runs On Whole Grain

after.name: Tir rapproché de Gnasher de Cole

incarnation.after: Gears of War 2 (2008), Dominic Santiago in Delta Squad armor

visualAnchor.after: Adult Dom with short dark hair, dark facial stubble, exposed muscular arms, grey-blue COG plates and blue lights. Carry Lancer Mk2/Gnasher as physical weapons; no Gears 3 grief-era long beard or supernatural Maria manifestation.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 2 (2008), Colonel Victor Hoffman during the Jacinto defense

visualAnchor.after: Older Colonel Victor Hoffman with weathered face, dark COG beret, heavy grey-blue officer armor and cyan armor lamps. A physical service firearm is carried; command orders do not project a holographic shield or summon soldiers.

after.name: Arme de service du colonel Hoffman
Ordre de défense du commandement COG
Ordre de mise en défense de Hoffman

incarnation.after: Gears 5 (2019), adult Kait in the winter COG field outfit

visualAnchor.after: Adult Kait with dark brown hair, practical grey-blue winter COG armor, a visible fur collar and a physical Lancer Mk3. Preserve the winter field silhouette rather than Gears 4 Outsider clothing, Locust anatomy or a supernatural Swarm attack.

after.name: Tir du Lancer Mk3 de Kait
Visée de terrain du Lancer de Kait

incarnation.after: Gears of War 2 (2008), Marcus Fenix in original Delta Squad armor

visualAnchor.after: Adult Marcus with a dark bandana, short dark hair, scarred square face, heavy grey-blue COG armor and cyan armor lights. His Lancer Mk2 has a firearm barrel and an attached chainsaw bayonet; no old-man beard, Gears 4 farm clothes or E-Day model.

incarnation.after: Gears 5 (2019), the Matriarch at the Mount Kadar laboratory

visualAnchor.after: The Gears 5 Matriarch is a massive blind, heavily plated female Locust with powerful forelimbs and a vulnerable exposed back. Target her laboratory/ice-arena form; do not reuse an ordinary 2006 Berserker, a Lambent Berserker or invented weapons.

incarnation.after: Gears of War (2006), Boomshot-equipped Boomer

visualAnchor.after: Very large heavyset pale Locust with a small head, thick exposed arms, heavy dark shoulder armor and a two-handed Boomshot grenade launcher. No Grinder minigun, Mauler shield or Berserker anatomy.

incarnation.after: Gears of War (2006), adult Corpser in the Imulsion mine

visualAnchor.after: Enormous subterranean arachnid-shaped Corpser with a recessed body, broad multi-eyed head and very long raised hooked digging limbs. Its source creature has no gun arms or dorsal missile pack; preserve adult rather than hatchling proportions.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 3 (2011), juvenile Corpser hatchling

visualAnchor.after: Small juvenile Corpser with a compact arachnid-like body, recessed head and long jointed digging limbs spreading around it. Keep the juvenile scale and bare creature anatomy; no adult armored head, Brumak guns or dorsal rocket rack.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 2 (2008), Locust explosive Ticker

visualAnchor.after: Low-slung squat Ticker with small eyes, tusk-like jaws, short scuttling legs and a visible explosive charge strapped to its back. Preserve the separate bomb harness; no wild unarmed Ticker or human suicide bomber anatomy.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 2 (2008), armed Brumak before Lambent mutation

visualAnchor.after: Huge grey reptilian Brumak with a separate Locust pilot, heavy metal harness, arm-mounted guns and a dorsal missile rack. No tentacles, glowing Imulsion growths or final Lambent Brumak form; Gargantuan is Nexus scaling, not a separate canonical species.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 2 (2008), Skorge at Nexus

visualAnchor.after: Skorge is a tall narrow Kantus leader with pale grey skin, an elongated head, dark reddish ceremonial armor and a double-ended chainsaw staff. No RAAM Troika, generic wizard staff or Reaver body fused into the character.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 2 (2008), standard Kantus priest

visualAnchor.after: Tall lean Kantus with long limbs, elongated head, dark reddish ceremonial armor/robes and a physical Gorgon pistol. Keep the narrow priest silhouette distinct from the bulky armored Kantus of Gears 3; no conjured staff or wings.

incarnation.after: Gears of War: Judgment (2013), Karn mounted on Shibboleth

visualAnchor.after: Karn is a pale armored Locust general positioned on the back of the large arachnid-like Shibboleth. Preserve rider and mount as distinct bodies; do not replace the mount with a Brumak or label Karn a generic sniper.

incarnation.after: Gears of War (2006), ordinary Locust Drone infantry

visualAnchor.after: Pale grey humanoid Locust Drone with a broad heavy head, thick neck, muscular stocky body, dark Locust harness/armor and a carried Hammerburst. No elite Theron cape, Swarm red tissue or Skaarj wrist blades.

incarnation.after: Gears of War (2006), non-Lambent Wretch

visualAnchor.after: Small hunched pale-grey Locust Wretch with long forelimbs, digitigrade hind limbs, clawed hands and a toothy head. It runs and climbs close to the ground; no gun, armor plates, Lambent yellow glow or explosive sac.

incarnation.after: Gears of War 3 (2011), Myrrah and the Tempest encounter

visualAnchor.after: Adult Myrrah is a pale human-looking queen with light hair and elaborate dark-gold Locust regalia. Her physical Tempest mount is a separate enormous winged creature; do not fuse its wings or limbs into Myrrah or borrow Skorge armor.

incarnation.after: Gears of War (2006), standard Theron Guard

visualAnchor.after: Tall Locust Theron Guard in ornate red-brown armor, distinctive crested helmet and draped coat/cape, carrying a physical Torque Bow. No unarmored Drone, later armored Kantus or RAAM-sized silhouette.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), Bill in his original Vietnam-veteran survivor outfit

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2008 Bill: older white human man, grey beard, green military beret, olive fatigue jacket and military trousers, with worn survivor gear. Keep him alive in the selected base-game survivor period, not a post-Sacrifice corpse or supernatural veteran.

after.name: Couvert de Bill derrière la barricade

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead 2 (2009), Coach in the original school-coach survivor outfit

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2 Coach: broad stocky Black human man with a bald head, two-tone purple-and-yellow school-coach shirt, dark trousers and sturdy shoes. Preserve his human proportions and civilian sporting outfit, without military armor or a transformed Tank body.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead 2 (2009), Ellis in the original mechanic survivor outfit

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2 Ellis: young adult white human mechanic, dark hair under a baseball cap, yellow work T-shirt and blue jeans. He is a human survivor with ordinary equipment, not a summoned repair robot or a Left 4 Dead 2008 cast member.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead 2 (2009), Nick in the original gambler survivor outfit

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2 Nick: adult white human man with short dark hair, white suit jacket and trousers over a blue open-neck shirt. Maintain the worn gambler survivor appearance and ordinary pistols; no military uniform or unique supernatural gun ability.

after.name: Retrait derrière les caisses avec Nick

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead 2 (2009), Rochelle in the original reporter survivor outfit

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2 Rochelle: adult Black human woman with tied-back dark hair, pink Depeche Mode T-shirt and dark trousers. Keep the base-game human reporter presentation, ordinary pistol and civilian clothes, with no laser or infected anatomy.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), Zoey in the original survivor outfit

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2008 Zoey: young adult human with dark ponytail, red zip-up jacket over a light shirt, dark jeans and trainers. Retain the original survivor outfit and physical firearm, not a sword, infected form or a later crossover costume.

after.name: Visée au fusil de chasse de Zoey

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), male Boomer special-infected model

visualAnchor.after: Original male Left 4 Dead Boomer: extremely swollen torso and belly, bloated human head, damaged civilian shirt and trousers, fluid-soiled body and short unstable posture. No female Boomette model or separate symbiotic host creature is selected.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), ordinary common infected civilian

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2008 common infected civilian: an aggressive human with disordered movement and damaged everyday clothing. This is an ordinary common-infected population target, not a uniform single named model, armored riot infected or a special-infected mutation.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), original Hunter during its pounce state

visualAnchor.after: Original Left 4 Dead hooded Hunter body during a crouch, leap or pinned attack, with dark sweatshirt and trousers and exposed hands and feet. Pounce names an action state, not another infected species or a different outfit.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), original Hunter special-infected model

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2008 Hunter: crouched hooded human infected in a dark hooded sweatshirt and trousers, low predatory posture, bare hands and feet. Keep the human hooded body and long-distance pounce, not an animal, firearm user or armored soldier.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), original Smoker special-infected model

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2008 Smoker: tall distorted human infected, large neck and facial growths, long prehensile tongue and torn civilian clothing. Preserve the original special-infected body; no conventional weapon or invented snake companion.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead 2 (2009), acid pool left by the Spitter special infected

visualAnchor.after: Left 4 Dead 2 Spitter acid pool: a spreading, bubbling green acidic patch on the ground. The selected source is the pool hazard, with no independent humanoid torso, face, arms, legs or hand-held acid gun.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), original Tank in a horde or rescue encounter

visualAnchor.after: Original Left 4 Dead Tank: massively overgrown bare upper body, enormous arms, small human head and torn trousers, with a forward heavy posture. Retain the original infected body without armor, artificial gauntlets or a second Witch body fused to it.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), original Witch seated in a dark corner

visualAnchor.after: Same original Left 4 Dead Witch body in its seated crying posture, long unkempt hair, elongated nails, bare feet and torn civilian clothes. The corner is encounter placement, not a new Witch species, costume or bride model.

incarnation.after: Left 4 Dead (2008), original seated Witch before being startled

visualAnchor.after: Original Left 4 Dead Witch: hunched human infected with long unkempt hair, pale damaged skin, very long claw-like fingernails, bare feet and torn civilian clothing, seated and crying before provocation. Not a bride, a daytime wandering sequel variant or a spell-casting witch.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), cooperative ATLAS test-robot chassis

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 ATLAS: short rounded spherical white shell, one blue optic, exposed dark joints, two arms and two legs, carrying the co-op portal device. Keep his compact body distinct from tall P-Body; no independent turret guns.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), human Caroline in the old-Aperture 1950s office portrait

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 human Caroline: adult human assistant with dark waved hair and period office clothing in the archival portrait. Do not replace her with a GLaDOS robotic shell, yellow mechanical optic or laser-wielding soldier; exact portrait coloring and facial resemblance remain pending visual review.

after.name: Caroline vérifie le dossier du laboratoire

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), Cave Johnson in the old-Aperture 1950s office portrait; human archival identity

visualAnchor.after: Cave Johnson in Portal 2 archival office material: adult human founder with dark hair and moustache in period business clothing. Keep an archival human presentation distinct from a personality sphere, robotic chassis or living present-day combatant; detailed portrait colors remain visually unverified.

after.name: Retrait vers la zone de test sûre

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), Cave Johnson 1980s old-Aperture audio recordings; legacy Echo alias has no independent canonical body

after.name: Rappeler la zone de test sûre

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), adult Chell in the single-player test chambers

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 adult Chell: dark ponytail, white Aperture tank top, orange jumpsuit tied at the waist, long-fall boots and the white-and-black dual portal device. Retain her human proportions; no Portal 1 closed jumpsuit, firearms, turret backpack or neurotoxin emitter.

incarnation.after: Portal 2: Lab Rat (2011), Doug Rattmann in the official bridge comic

visualAnchor.after: Official Lab Rat Doug Rattmann: dishevelled human scientist with unkempt hair, beard and lab clothing, linked to hand-drawn wall murals, hidden routes and the Companion Cube. Preserve the comic human identity; the cube is a prop, not a new limb or a combat terminal.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), GLaDOS in her central chamber chassis

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 GLaDOS central chassis: suspended white and black segmented mechanical assembly, a yellow optic and ceiling-connected cables and supports. No humanoid legs, portable flight, potato shell or Portal 1 personality-core cluster in this selected form.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), GLaDOS carried as PotatOS after Wheatley transfers her to a potato battery

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 PotatOS: an irregular brown potato battery carrying GLaDOS electronics, a yellow optic, wires and clips. It is a small physical prop carried with the portal device, not a humanoid, full central chassis or armed hovering core.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), cooperative P-Body test-robot chassis

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 P-Body: tall narrow oval white shell, orange optic, long slender articulated legs and arms with dark joints; co-op portal device held as test equipment. Do not substitute the short spherical ATLAS body.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), Wheatley personality sphere before central-chassis transfer

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 Wheatley personality sphere: white spherical casing, single blue optic, black side handles and articulated eye mount. Use his core form held or attached to facility rails; no Wheatley central chassis, independent combat-drone wings or gun.

incarnation.after: Portal (2007), standard Aperture floor sentry turret

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2007 floor turret: white teardrop shell, black inner frame, one red optic, three narrow support legs and side-mounted gun assemblies. It is a grounded machine, not a humanoid carrying a rifle.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), defective turret from the turret manufacturing line

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 defective turret: exposed dark internal frame, red optic and incomplete or absent white outer shell, on narrow turret supports. Do not render an ordinary complete white sentry just because both have red eyes.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), Excursion Funnel transport volume

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 Excursion Funnel: a projected blue transport funnel emitted from an installed circular apparatus; reversing changes its flow and presentation. Render the beam and its fixture as environment, with no face, arms, legs or separate creature body.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), Fact Core attached during the final corrupted-core sequence

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 Fact Core: small white spherical personality-core casing with its distinct colored optic and handles. It speaks incorrect facts; no humanoid body, independent combat drone or physical logic-snare apparatus is established.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), Wheatley turret-and-weighted-cube hybrid

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 Frankenturret: a weighted cube combined with visibly awkward turret components and thin mechanical legs. Preserve the cube-and-turret construction rather than inventing a humanoid robot; detailed assembly and lens positions require the pending model review.

incarnation.after: Portal (2007), GLaDOS in the central AI chamber before core detachment

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2007 GLaDOS: ceiling-suspended white and black central machinery, yellow optic, facility cables and detachable personality cores. Keep this machine form distinct from Portal 2 central GLaDOS, Wheatley and the potato battery.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), installed gel distribution apparatus in old Aperture tests

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 environmental gel apparatus: installed industrial pipes, outlets and colored test-gel splashes on chamber surfaces. There is no gel-pump humanoid, independent face or hand-held gel cannon.

incarnation.after: Portal (2007), central AI chamber neurotoxin ventilation hazard

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2007 chamber hazard: installed air ducts, ventilation grilles and facility-connected machinery. Represent an environmental system and timer, not a separate green monster or humanoid boss.

incarnation.after: Portal (2007), fixed rocket sentry in Aperture test and central-AI chambers

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2007 rocket turret: fixed industrial launcher head, dark mechanical mounting and tracking optic, attached to facility structure. Keep it distinct from the three-legged bullet sentry.

incarnation.after: Portal (2007), rocket-turret mechanism; Prototype is the legacy encounter label

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2007 fixed rocket turret apparatus, with mechanical mount, launcher and tracking optic. The legacy Prototype suffix does not establish an extra canonical model or a different armed robot body.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), Space Core in the final corrupted-core sequence

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 Space Core: small white spherical personality-core shell, optic and handles, with excited dialogue about space. Keep the detached core body; no wings, vacuum generator or gravitational limbs.

incarnation.after: Portal 2 (2011), Wheatley after transfer into the central AI chassis

visualAnchor.after: Portal 2 central Wheatley: the large suspended white-and-black central machine assembly now carrying his blue optic. It is distinct from the small rail-mounted personality sphere and does not gain a human body.
